conservative.headline: Partisan Stunt: Democrats Launch Political Witch Hunt Against DHS Secretary Doing Her Job
conservative.byline: As seen on Fox News, Washington Examiner, The Hill
paragraphs: House Democrats are launching yet another partisan impeachment crusade—this time targeting the Homeland Security Secretary who's actually securing our border.

Secretary Kristi Noem faces mounting calls for impeachment from Democrats following two incidents in Minneapolis where federal immigration enforcement officers shot and killed individuals during enforcement operations. More than 160 House Democrats have signed onto impeachment articles introduced by Rep. Robin Kelly of Illinois.

But President Trump isn't backing down. When asked Tuesday if Noem would step down, he said plainly "no" and defended her performance: "I do. Who closed up the border? She did, with [Border Czar] Tom Homan, with the whole group." He added that Noem is "doing a very good job."

House Republicans are calling out the impeachment effort for what it is: pure partisan politics. Rep. Andy Biggs blasted the resolution as "a partisan stunt with no factual or constitutional basis" and noted Democrats "couldn't even unify their own caucus behind it."

Secretary Noem defended the federal agents' actions, explaining that the situation in Minneapolis involved violent resistance. She characterized the incidents as meeting the legal definition of domestic terrorism, stating: "When you perpetuate violence against a government because of ideological reasons, that is the definition of domestic terrorism."

This isn't about accountability—it's about Democrats trying to sabotage effective border enforcement. Secretary Noem is doing exactly what the American people elected President Trump to do, and Democrats can't stand it.

liberal.headline: Blood on Her Hands: Secretary Noem Must Be Fired or Impeached After Lying About Fatal Shootings
liberal.byline: As seen on NBC News, Washington Post, CBS News
paragraphs: Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem lied about federal agents killing two U.S. citizens in Minneapolis—and now she must face consequences.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries delivered an ultimatum to President Trump on Tuesday: fire Noem immediately, or Democrats will impeach her. "We will commence impeachment proceedings against Kristi Noem in the absence of her being fired," Jeffries stated on CNN.

In a written statement, Jeffries added: "Kristi Noem should be fired immediately, or we will commence impeachment proceedings in the House of Representatives. We can do this the easy way or the hard way." He told reporters in the Capitol: "She needs to be put on ice permanently."

Rep. Robin Kelly of Illinois, who introduced the impeachment articles, didn't mince words: "Secretary Kristi Noem is an incompetent leader, a disgrace to our democracy, and I am impeaching her for obstruction of justice, violation of public trust, and self-dealing."

The impeachment push gained steam after Border Patrol agents fatally shot Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old ICU nurse, in Minneapolis on January 24. Video footage directly contradicted Noem's claims that Pretti "attacked" officers—the video shows Pretti holding a cellphone, not a weapon, before agents confiscated his legally-owned firearm from his waistband and then shot him.

Even some Republicans are breaking ranks. Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina became the first GOP senator to call for Noem's removal, stating: "What she's done in Minnesota should be disqualifying. She should be out of a job." He added: "It's just amateur-ish. It's terrible. It's making the president look bad on policy that he won on."

Over 160 House Democrats—three-quarters of the Democratic caucus—have now signed onto the impeachment resolution. The charges include obstruction of justice for denying members of Congress access to ICE facilities, violation of public trust for ordering warrantless arrests and excessive force, and self-dealing for allegedly misusing $200 million for ICE recruitment ads.
Two U.S. citizens are dead because of Kristi Noem's incompetence, and then she lied about what happened. If Trump won't fire her, Congress must remove her.

factcheck.headline: What Actually Happened in Minneapolis—And What Comes Next
paragraphs: The impeachment push centers on two fatal shootings in Minneapolis and disputed claims about what happened. Here's what we actually know.
THE UNDISPUTED FACTS:

✓ Two U.S. citizens were killed by federal agents in Minneapolis in January 2026: Renée Nicole Good was shot on January 7 by an ICE officer. Alex Pretti, a 37-year-old ICU nurse, was shot on January 24 by Border Patrol agents. Both were U.S. citizens protesting immigration enforcement operations.

✓ Video contradicts Noem's initial account: Secretary Noem claimed Pretti "attacked" officers and brandished a gun. However, video footage verified by ABC News shows Pretti holding a cellphone, not a weapon. Agents can be seen confiscating Pretti's legally-owned firearm from his waistband before shots were fired. Ten shots were fired total, with six shots fired at Pretti's motionless body.
✓ 162 House Democrats have signed impeachment articles: Rep. Robin Kelly introduced the resolution on January 14. As of January 28, three-quarters of House Democrats back the effort.

✓ Impeachment articles allege three charges: (1) Obstruction of justice for denying congressional access to ICE facilities, (2) Violation of public trust for ordering warrantless arrests and excessive force, (3) Self-dealing for allegedly misusing $200 million for ICE recruitment advertising.
✓ Trump is standing by Noem: When asked if she would step down, Trump said "no" and stated she's doing a "very good job."
CONSERVATIVE SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Claim: "Partisan stunt with no factual basis" — The video evidence directly contradicts Noem's public statements about what happened. Whether that rises to "high crimes and misdemeanors" warranting impeachment is a political judgment, but the factual discrepancies are real.

✓ Fair Point: Democrats don't have the votes. With Republicans controlling the House, at least three GOP members would need to vote with all Democrats to impeach—which is highly unlikely. Even if the House did impeach, conviction in the Senate would require a two-thirds majority (67 votes), which is virtually impossible.

⚠️ Claim: Pretti "perpetuated violence" and committed "domestic terrorism" — Video shows Pretti holding a phone, not attacking anyone. An internal Border Patrol review obtained by NPR makes no mention of Pretti attacking officers or threatening them with a weapon. Calling a U.S. citizen exercising First and Second Amendment rights a "domestic terrorist" is inflammatory and unsupported by the evidence.
LIBERAL SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Claim: Noem has "blood on her hands" — While Noem's public statements were inaccurate, there's no evidence she personally ordered either shooting. The agents who fired the shots made split-second decisions in the field. Whether Noem's leadership created conditions that led to these deaths is a legitimate question, but the "blood on her hands" framing oversimplifies a complex situation.

✓ Fair Point: Noem did make demonstrably false public statements. She claimed Pretti "attacked" officers when video shows otherwise. She called his actions "domestic terrorism" without evidence. As the secretary overseeing these agencies, accountability for false public statements is a legitimate issue.

⚠️ Claim: This impeachment is about accountability, not politics — The timing and party-line nature suggest politics is a major factor. If this were purely about accountability, you'd see more bipartisan support. Only two Republican senators (Tillis and Murkowski) have called for Noem's resignation, and no House Republicans have signed the impeachment articles.
THE BIGGER PICTURE:

This case raises fundamental questions about federal law enforcement, accountability, and truth-telling by cabinet officials. Two U.S. citizens are dead. Video evidence contradicts the official account. The question isn't whether these deaths are tragic—they clearly are. The question is who bears responsibility and what consequences should follow.

On one hand: Federal agents face dangerous, split-second decisions during enforcement operations. Hindsight is always clearer than real-time judgment. Border security is a legitimate government function.

On the other hand: When a cabinet secretary makes public statements that video evidence contradicts, accountability matters. When federal agents kill U.S. citizens and the official story doesn't match the video, transparency matters. When 162 elected representatives from across the country call for impeachment, their concerns deserve consideration.

The Bottom Line: The impeachment effort is politically motivated AND based on legitimate concerns about false statements. These aren't mutually exclusive. Whether you think Noem should be impeached likely depends on whether you think her false statements about the shootings constitute "high crimes and misdemeanors"—or whether you think Democrats are exploiting tragic events for political gain. Both interpretations have evidence to support them.
